sources.entry: NeatEditor - Fast, native macOS plain-text editor for distraction-free writing. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/NeatMacApps/NeatEditor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: NeatEditor is a minimal, fast-launching native macOS plain-text editor built with SwiftUI and AppKit for distraction-free multi-tab writing.
summary.what_it_does: NeatEditor is a plain-text editor for macOS that opens with a ready-to-use document and supports multiple tabs with selection, closing, reopening closed tabs, and in-place renaming. It can open local text files via Finder, drag and drop, or pasted file URLs. The editor includes line numbers, native find, undo, IME composition handling, and Command +/- zooming. Changes are autosaved on a debounce, on tab switch, and when the app deactivates, and blank content is designed never to overwrite existing files. New app-created documents are stored in ~/Documents by default, with the folder configurable in Settings.
use_cases: writing quick notes and scratch text on a Mac
editing several text files in tabs
keeping a pinned on-top scratchpad window
how_to_run: Download a signed DMG from GitHub Releases (check the release notes state Developer ID-signed + notarized), open it, and drag NeatEditor.app to Applications.
git clone the repository and cd NeatEditor
notable: Conflict-safe saving: external changes reload clean buffers, independent edits merge conservatively, and conflicting edits keep both versions
Ordered saves prevent an older autosave from overwriting a newer save
Disk-backed rename preserves editable file extensions
Documents folder is configurable and older app-library documents are copied over on first launch
Universal build for Apple silicon and Intel
caveats: Requires macOS 26.0+ and Xcode 26.0+ to build from source; Linux and Windows are not supported
Plain text only: no rich text, plugins, or cross-platform support
Public installs come from a local signed release route; older unsigned universal assets should not be installed
README notes limits on safety and verification and states no delivery is claimed as verified beyond release notes and checksums
